cells.tense: You are here holding the pen, before any choice settles this.
cells.act: make something skilled and small on the cleared ground
cells.ask: Make one small skilled thing on cleared ground this season — start it, finish it, and plan no use for it. The point is the making, and then putting it down.
cells.core: The pen is in your hand and nothing is decided. That's the whole advantage: you can draw on everything you know without choosing one road, and the one clear piece still reaches the person who needs it next. It goes out because it is ready, not because you are ahead of anyone. The not-yet is where range lives, and it isn't wasted time. You don't have to commit in order to prove you have range, and you don't have to narrow anything down before the shape is there. Build one small good thing on the cleared ground. Look at what you made. Leave the next choice where it is. What you make now carries visible edges, and that is enough.
cells.sheetLine: You can shape one true thing before anything is chosen.
cells.verb: charting a way through for people who can't yet see it
cells.place: the moment before choice, where everything is still possible

cells.tense: You'll be rehearsing the handoff before there is anything to hand over.
cells.act: let the friction test what you are committed to
cells.ask: Take the hardest part of one thing near you on purpose, without coping first, and stay with it until you can tell what you're actually committed to — then decide nothing at all.
cells.core: Where the showing happens after the work is finished, the work is real and the people being led can feel it. The trouble sits in the space between. Bracing ahead, the clearing gets finished before anything has grown, and guiding people gets rehearsed before there is a path to guide them down. Boats multiply; the water stays uncrossed. You are standing where the guiding goes, reading the speech to a room that hasn't arrived. The people you'd lead can feel the gap between the direction and the thing being directed at. Friction is information, not failure — it tells you which commitment is real. Let one hard thing test you before you decide what it means, instead of deciding first and reaching for the first hard thing that agrees.

cells.tense: You were someone people followed once, and that door sits behind you.
cells.act: keep your own count of what is owed, and pay it
cells.ask: Keep your own count of one small thing owed — a debt, a favor, a wrong — and pay it before anyone asks. Stop there, with nothing added.
cells.core: When your sense of what's owed is moving, you settle it without fanfare: a small debt cleared, a wrong quietly set right, and the room gets lighter without anyone knowing why. It reaches your hands before it reaches your mouth. Here it isn't moving at all. Something plainly unfair goes past and nothing in you stands up to walk toward it. That's not a lack of judgment — you can still read what's owed. What's gone is the purchase behind the reading. You don't have to feel fair first, and you don't have to want to. One small right, done in private, shows you the machinery still turns.
cells.sheetLine: You can still see what's fair. You've stopped calling it.

cells.tense: You are steering while the room you write from isn't yours.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Join one person in a piece of work you can share this week, side by side in the same task, and stay with the joint version instead of correcting it back to yours.
cells.core: When the direction works and is claimed, you and another move toward the same thing, and the work carries both of you instead of you carrying it while they watch. Here, the true account — the one where you chose the course, held it steady, adjusted when it drifted — is not the account being told, and the version they carry leaves your hand out of it. Nothing is missing in what you know. What's missing is your name on the part you did. Meeting someone in the middle, once, on something small, shows the shape of it: not you pushing a plan onto them, not you disappearing behind theirs. You step. They step. Both of you see who moved.

A reader could fairly say the door is still theirs and not behind them — the ask is written so it survives that: it is one unshown mark, and the fairness holds whether or not the reader accepts the location reading. The sentence serving me rather than them is the door and threshold imagery; it is cut or carried once as a life-image, not repeated.
